clue.text: Wrong to regale one's other half?

indicators.note: something gone wrong is out of order, so the following letters are put back in a different arrangement

blocks.note: the two words supply the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A spouse being told it is wrong to entertain someone with lavish stories.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's other half' usually means a spouse, but here it is the second self.
explanation.definitionFit: An alter ego is a second self, the hidden other side of a person's character.

clue.text: Course of action, after a time, becomes offensive

indicators.note: after sends the course of action to follow the other pieces rather than lead

blocks.note: taken as written
T is the standard abbreviation for time
a tack is a course of action, as in trying a different tack

explanation.surface: A plan of action that, given time, turns aggressive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts the course of action behind A and T. Here 'offensive' is the noun, a military push.
explanation.definitionFit: An offensive is a military campaign of assault, which is an attack.

clue.text: Pain of the first artist with a university degree

indicators.note: first asks for the opening letter only of the word that follows it

blocks.note: the opening letter of 'the'
RA, Royal Academician, is the usual crossword artist
U is the abbreviation for university
MA is a Master of Arts degree

explanation.surface: The suffering of a pioneering painter who also holds an academic qualification.
explanation.definitionFit: Trauma is severe emotional or physical hurt, a synonym for deep pain.

clue.text: Careless about girl

blocks.note: re means about or concerning
a miss is a girl or young woman

explanation.surface: Someone being casual and negligent where a young woman is concerned.
explanation.definitionFit: Remiss means negligent in one's duty, which is to be careless.

clue.text: Go away — as consumer will do with journalist

blocks.note: a consumer acquires goods, that is, obtains things
ED, short for editor, is the usual crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A rude dismissal, linked to what a shopper does along with a reporter.
explanation.walkthrough: GET STUFF is what a consumer does; ED is added. The answer is a rude British phrase telling someone to clear off.
explanation.definitionFit: Get stuffed is a rude British exclamation meaning clear off, an idiomatic order to leave.

clue.text: Doubled up and collapsed

blocks.note: first meaning: bent over on itself, as paper is creased
second meaning: failed, as a business that has gone under

explanation.surface: Someone bent over in pain who then fell down.
explanation.definitionFit: Paper creased over is folded, and a failed business is said to have folded.

clue.text: Finished with boyfriend daughter finds square

blocks.note: out means over or finished
a date is the person one is going out with
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A girl who has dumped her boyfriend finds him dull and conventional.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Square' is slang for old-fashioned, not a shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Square in slang means old-fashioned and conventional, which is outdated.

clue.text: Tedious tie-in finally revealed

indicators.note: finally keeps only the closing letter of the word before it

blocks.note: a tie in a match is a draw
the last letter of 'in'
a secret that is out has been revealed

explanation.surface: A boring promotional product finally unveiled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tie-in' looks like one word for merchandise, but tie and in are used separately.
explanation.definitionFit: Something drawn-out is prolonged beyond its interest, hence tedious.

clue.text: Workers in period dress

blocks.note: a day is a period of time
a shift is a loose straight dress

explanation.surface: Workers wearing costume from a historical era.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Period dress' suggests historical costume; the words are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The day shift is the group of employees who work during daytime hours.

clue.text: Colleague has a drink before Mamet play

indicators.note: to play with something is to toy with it, so the letters are moved around

blocks.note: tea is a drink
the playwright's name, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A co-worker has a cuppa before watching a play by David Mamet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mamet play' suggests a work by the American dramatist, but play is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A team-mate is a fellow member of a working team, so a colleague.

clue.text: Set off at daybreak when calm

indicators.note: off suggests being out of place, so letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
day broken up: the word day, with break telling you to mix it in with the rest

explanation.surface: Setting out at dawn when the weather is still.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daybreak' splits: day is fodder and break joins off in signalling the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Steady means stable and composed, a synonym for calm.

clue.text: Flower found by quiet place used by travellers

blocks.note: a flower is something that flows, a river; the Cam runs through Cambridge
p, piano, is the musical mark for quiet
a site is a place

explanation.surface: A flower discovered beside a peaceful spot that travellers use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' means a river here, not a bloom. 'Place' serves both the definition and the last piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A campsite is ground where travellers and holidaymakers pitch tents or caravans.

clue.text: Bend to accept a piece of meat

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it in, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: to hunch is to bend the back
taken as written

explanation.surface: Stooping down to receive a cut of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: A haunch is the leg and loin of an animal, a joint served as meat, as in haunch of venison.

clue.text: Revealing act

blocks.note: surface reading: a deed that discloses a secret
setter's reading: a stage performance in which the performer shows more and more skin

explanation.walkthrough: 'Revealing' suggests disclosure, but the act literally reveals the body.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a burlesque performance where clothes are removed slowly, so it literally exposes the body.

clue.text: Unprepared, having cancelled the buffet

blocks.note: an event called off is cancelled
taken as written
to buffet is to strike, as a cuff is a blow

explanation.surface: Someone unready because the buffet meal was called off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buffet' looks like a spread of food but is the verb to hit.
explanation.definitionFit: Off the cuff means spoken without rehearsal, improvised and unprepared.

clue.text: Shocking events as boy turned up during examinations

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned up means read from bottom to top
during places one item within the time span of the other, so inside it

blocks.note: a lad is a boy
scans are medical examinations

explanation.surface: Outrage as a boy shows up while tests are being sat.
explanation.definitionFit: Scandals are disgraceful happenings that cause public outrage.

clue.text: Unconnected to the musician

blocks.note: surface reading: detached or unrelated in general
setter's reading: the word a player uses for notes played short and detached from one another

explanation.walkthrough: 'To the musician' tells you to read 'unconnected' as a term of musical performance.
explanation.definitionFit: In music, the term marks notes played sharply detached from each other, rather than smoothly joined.

clue.text: Bliss of being level against a foreign side

indicators.note: foreign suggests something made strange, so the letters are put in an unfamiliar order

blocks.note: at par means level or equal
taken as written
the letters of side rearranged

explanation.surface: The joy of drawing level in a match with a team from abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Paradise is a state of supreme happiness, so bliss.

clue.text: Example of home cooking?

blocks.note: surface reading: any homely dish made in a domestic kitchen
setter's reading: a baked dish named after a small rural house, so literally a home's food

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'home' points to the dwelling in the dish's name.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a classic British dish of minced meat topped with mashed potato, typical family fare.

clue.text: Empty tin inside a large container

indicators.note: inside puts the first item within the second

blocks.note: a tin is a can
a vat is a large tank or tub

explanation.surface: An empty tin sitting inside a big tank.
explanation.definitionFit: Vacant means unoccupied, with nothing in it, so empty.

clue.text: Relaxed with a joke

blocks.note: taken as written
to tease is to joke with someone

explanation.surface: Someone loosened up by a bit of humour.
explanation.definitionFit: To be at ease is to feel comfortable and free from tension.

clue.text: Many attempt to get over the French girl

indicators.note: to get over is to be turned over, so in a down entry the word reads upwards

blocks.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so many
a try is an attempt
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Lots of people trying to win over a French girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get over' sounds like recovering from someone, but it turns the attempt upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: Myrtle is a woman's given name, so it stands for a girl.

clue.text: Caught in close embrace — it's delicious

definitions.note: the answer is a noun, something delicious

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold in one's arms, so one piece wraps round the other

blocks.note: close means near
ct is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Someone captured in a tight hug, finding it wonderful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close embrace' looks like a hug; close is the outer word and embrace the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Nectar, the drink of the gods, is any delightfully sweet and tasty drink.

clue.text: Secret way to sound less hard

indicators.note: less means without, and hard is H in pencil grading, so that letter goes

blocks.note: St, street, is a way
sound means in good health

explanation.surface: A clandestine method to make something seem softer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' here is the adjective meaning fit and well, not a noise.
explanation.definitionFit: Stealthy means done quietly and covertly, so as not to be noticed, which is secret.

clue.text: Nearly saying I love a piece of music

indicators.note: nearly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: an adage is a saying
taken as written
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: Almost declaring affection for a musical work.
explanation.definitionFit: An adagio is a slow movement or composition, so a piece of music.

clue.text: It stops one seeing waterfall

blocks.note: first meaning: a clouding of the eye's lens
second meaning: a large, steep cascade

explanation.surface: A torrent of water so heavy that it blocks the view.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an eye condition clouding the lens and a large steep waterfall.

clue.text: Lost out by a couple of points won by luck

indicators.note: out suggests being dislodged from place, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
E and N are two compass points, east and north

explanation.surface: A narrow defeat by two points in a game won through fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lost' looks like the definition, but it is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A victory gained undeservedly or by fortune is said to be stolen, as in a stolen win.

clue.text: Foolishly tease the art lover

indicators.note: acting foolishly is behaving without order, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the two words supply the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Mocking someone who enjoys art, in a silly way.
explanation.definitionFit: An aesthete is a person with refined appreciation of beauty and the arts.
